rows: Render a bar chart from an input relation to a PNG image BLOB (JFreeChart). With a series column, bars are grouped per series value.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Render a **bar chart** as a PNG image `BLOB` from a DuckDB relation. Name the `category` column (the discrete x-axis groups) and the numeric `value` column; supply an optional `series` column to draw grouped bars (one colored bar per series value within each category), plus optional `title`, `width`, and `height`.

Use it to compare a numeric measure across discrete categories — for example counts per status, revenue per quarter, or units per product. Rows with a NULL category or value are skipped. Returns a single `(png BLOB)` row holding the rendered PNG.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## chart_bar

Render a **vertical bar chart** from a query result to a PNG image `BLOB`.

### Usage

Pass the relation as the table argument, name the `category` and `value` columns, and optionally add a `series` column plus `title`, `width`, and `height`. See this function's example queries for complete, runnable calls.

### Notes

- One bar per category; with `series`, bars are grouped per series value.
- The `value` column must be numeric; NULL category/value rows are ignored.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Render one bar per category and report the PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_bar((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('A', 30), ('B', 45), ('C', 12)) AS t(category, value)), category := 'category', value := 'value', title := 'Counts')"},{"description":"Render grouped bars (one group per product series) of units by quarter.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_bar((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Q1', 30, 'Widget'), ('Q2', 42, 'Widget'), ('Q1', 18, 'Gadget'), ('Q2', 25, 'Gadget')) AS t(quarter, units, product)), category := 'quarter', value := 'units', series := 'product', title := 'Units per quarter by product')"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"png","type":"BLOB","description":"The rendered chart as a PNG image (raw bytes), ready to write to a .png file with DuckDB's COPY, embed in HTML, or hand to an image viewer."}]
rows.vgi.title: Bar Chart Renderer

rows: Render a histogram of a numeric column to a PNG image BLOB (JFreeChart), binning the values into `bins` equal-width buckets.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Render a **histogram** as a PNG image `BLOB` from a DuckDB relation. Name the numeric `value` column and optionally set `bins` (the number of equal-width buckets, default 20), plus optional `title`, `width`, and `height`.

Use it to visualize the distribution of a single numeric variable — latencies, prices, measurement spreads — by counting how many values fall into each bucket between the observed min and max. Rows with a NULL value are skipped; `bins` <= 0 falls back to 20. Returns a single `(png BLOB)` row holding the rendered PNG.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## chart_histogram

Render a **histogram** of a numeric column to a PNG image `BLOB`.

### Usage

Pass the relation as the table argument, name the numeric `value` column, and optionally set `bins` plus `title`, `width`, and `height`. See this function's example queries for complete, runnable calls.

### Notes

- Values are binned into `bins` equal-width buckets across the observed range.
- `value` must be numeric; NULL values are ignored and `bins <= 0` defaults to 20.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Bin five values into 5 equal-width buckets and report the PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_histogram((SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1.0), (1.5), (2.0), (2.0), (3.5)) AS t(value)), value := 'value', bins := 5, title := 'Distribution')"},{"description":"Render a 30-bucket histogram of request latency as a 900x500 PNG.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_histogram((SELECT * FROM (VALUES (12.0), (15.0), (15.0), (22.0), (30.0), (45.0), (9.0)) AS t(latency_ms)), value := 'latency_ms', bins := 30, title := 'Latency distribution', width := 900, height := 500)"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"png","type":"BLOB","description":"The rendered chart as a PNG image (raw bytes), ready to write to a .png file with DuckDB's COPY, embed in HTML, or hand to an image viewer."}]
rows.vgi.title: Histogram Chart Renderer

rows: Render a line chart from an input relation to a PNG image BLOB (JFreeChart). With a series column, one line per series value.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Render a **line chart** as a PNG image `BLOB` from a DuckDB relation. Pass the relation as the table argument and name the `x` and `y` columns; supply an optional `series` column to draw one line per distinct series value, and optional `title`, `width`, and `height`.

Use it when you have an ordered or time-like x axis and want to show a trend or compare several series over a common x. The x axis is numeric when the x column is numeric (including `DATE` / `TIMESTAMP` / `DECIMAL`), otherwise it becomes a category axis. Rows where x or y is NULL are skipped. Returns a single `(png BLOB)` row holding the rendered PNG.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## chart_line

Render a **line chart** from a query result to a PNG image `BLOB`.

### Usage

Pass the relation as the table argument, name the `x` and `y` columns, and optionally add a `series` column plus `title`, `width`, and `height`. See this function's example queries for complete, runnable calls.

### Notes

- A numeric x column yields a numeric axis; a text x column yields a category axis.
- With `series`, one line is drawn per distinct series value.
- Rows with NULL x or y are ignored; an empty relation yields no rows.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Render a single line over numeric x/y points and report the PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_line((SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1, 10), (2, 25), (3, 18), (4, 30)) AS t(x, y)), x := 'x', y := 'y', title := 'Trend')"},{"description":"Render one line per region (series) of revenue over months and report its PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_line((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Jan', 100, 'East'), ('Feb', 140, 'East'), ('Jan', 80, 'West'), ('Feb', 95, 'West')) AS t(month, revenue, region)), x := 'month', y := 'revenue', series := 'region', title := 'Revenue by region')"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description":"Render a single line over numeric x/y points and report the PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_line((SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1, 10), (2, 25), (3, 18), (4, 30)) AS t(x, y)), x := 'x', y := 'y', title := 'Trend')"},{"description":"Render one line per region (series) of revenue over months and report its PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_line((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Jan', 100, 'East'), ('Feb', 140, 'East'), ('Jan', 80, 'West'), ('Feb', 95, 'West')) AS t(month, revenue, region)), x := 'month', y := 'revenue', series := 'region', title := 'Revenue by region')"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"png","type":"BLOB","description":"The rendered chart as a PNG image (raw bytes), ready to write to a .png file with DuckDB's COPY, embed in HTML, or hand to an image viewer."}]

rows: Render a pie chart from an input relation to a PNG image BLOB (JFreeChart). One slice per distinct label; duplicate labels are summed.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Render a **pie chart** as a PNG image `BLOB` from a DuckDB relation. Name the `label` column (slice names) and the numeric `value` column (slice sizes); supply optional `title`, `width`, and `height`.

Use it to show the composition of a whole — market share, budget split, or category proportions. There is one slice per distinct label, and rows that share a label are summed into a single slice. Rows with a NULL label or value are skipped. Returns a single `(png BLOB)` row holding the rendered PNG.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## chart_pie

Render a **pie chart** from a query result to a PNG image `BLOB`.

### Usage

Pass the relation as the table argument, name the `label` and `value` columns, and optionally add a `title`, `width`, and `height`. See this function's example queries for complete, runnable calls.

### Notes

- One slice per distinct label; duplicate labels are summed.
- `value` must be numeric; NULL label/value rows are ignored.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Render a pie with one slice per label and report the PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_pie((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Chrome', 65), ('Safari', 19), ('Firefox', 16)) AS t(label, value)), label := 'label', value := 'value', title := 'Browser share')"},{"description":"Render spend per category as a 700x700 pie (duplicate categories are summed).","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_pie((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Rent', 1200), ('Food', 450), ('Rent', 100), ('Travel', 300)) AS t(category, amount)), label := 'category', value := 'amount', title := 'Spend by category', width := 700, height := 700)"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"png","type":"BLOB","description":"The rendered chart as a PNG image (raw bytes), ready to write to a .png file with DuckDB's COPY, embed in HTML, or hand to an image viewer."}]

rows: Render a scatter plot from an input relation to a PNG image BLOB (JFreeChart). With a series column, one point series per series value.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Render a **scatter plot** as a PNG image `BLOB` from a DuckDB relation. Name the numeric `x` and `y` columns; supply an optional `series` column to draw one colored point series per distinct series value, plus optional `title`, `width`, and `height`.

Use it to inspect the relationship or correlation between two numeric variables, or to compare clusters across groups via the series column. Both x and y must be numeric; rows with NULL x or y are skipped. Returns a single `(png BLOB)` row holding the rendered PNG.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## chart_scatter

Render a **scatter plot** from a query result to a PNG image `BLOB`.

### Usage

Pass the relation as the table argument, name the numeric `x` and `y` columns, and optionally add a `series` column plus `title`, `width`, and `height`. See this function's example queries for complete, runnable calls.

### Notes

- Both `x` and `y` must be numeric.
- With `series`, one point series is drawn per distinct value; NULL x/y rows are ignored.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Render a scatter plot of numeric x/y points and report the PNG byte size.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_scatter((SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1.0, 2.1), (2.0, 3.9), (3.0, 6.2)) AS t(x, y)), x := 'x', y := 'y', title := 'x vs y')"},{"description":"Render one colored point series per cohort of height against weight.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(png) AS bytes FROM chart.main.chart_scatter((SELECT * FROM (VALUES (170.0, 65.0, 'A'), (180.0, 80.0, 'A'), (160.0, 55.0, 'B'), (175.0, 72.0, 'B')) AS t(height_cm, weight_kg, cohort)), x := 'height_cm', y := 'weight_kg', series := 'cohort', title := 'Height vs weight by cohort')"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"png","type":"BLOB","description":"The rendered chart as a PNG image (raw bytes), ready to write to a .png file with DuckDB's COPY, embed in HTML, or hand to an image viewer."}]

rows: List every chart function this worker exposes, with its category, a one-line summary, and the named column arguments it takes.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: List every chart function this worker exposes — `chart_line`, `chart_bar`, `chart_pie`, `chart_scatter`, and `chart_histogram` — each with its category, a one-line summary of what it visualizes, and the named column arguments it takes. Query it to discover which chart type fits your data and what columns to name before calling a chart function, or to drive a chart-type picker. Takes no arguments and always returns one row per chart type.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## chart_types

A reference table with one row per chart function this worker exposes, so you can discover the available chart types and their inputs before calling one.

Each row gives the function's SQL name, its category, a one-line summary of what it visualizes, and the named column arguments it accepts. Takes no arguments and always returns rows.

See this object's example queries for complete, runnable calls.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"List every chart type this worker offers with its category and the column arguments it takes.","sql":"SELECT chart_type, category, column_arguments FROM chart.main.chart_types() ORDER BY chart_type"},{"description":"Find the chart types that compare a measure across discrete categories.","sql":"SELECT chart_type, summary FROM chart.main.chart_types() WHERE category = 'categorical-comparisons' ORDER BY chart_type"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description":"List every chart type with its category, ordered by name.","sql":"SELECT chart_type, category FROM chart.main.chart_types() ORDER BY chart_type"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"chart_type","type":"VARCHAR","description":"The chart function's SQL name, e.g. chart_line."},{"name":"category","type":"VARCHAR","description":"The chart's category in the schema's category registry."},{"name":"summary","type":"VARCHAR","description":"One-line description of what the chart visualizes."},{"name":"column_arguments","type":"VARCHAR","description":"The named column arguments that select the data to plot, in call order."}]
